citations.assessment: Tosafot gives thirteen thousand in its account of the deposit. This supports the opening figure as an attested reading despite the twelve thousand in the digital Bava Batra.
The digital Bavli gives twelve thousand before the birth and academy wording.
The two different statuses explicitly refer to conception and birth.
Rashbam gives Rachel’s name, relationship and the chronology.
Ketubot gives the daughters’ captivity. The identification of Rachel here comes from Rashbam.
The legal argument about this acquisition belongs to Rava’s voice.
Rashbam supplies Rava’s first-person explanation of possession and priority. It is commentary on this argument.
Rav Ika son of Rav Ammi proposes acknowledgment. The document then goes out from Issur and Rava objects.
Tosafot asks why Rava would not remit the deposit under the interpretation that the sages favor repayment. Rabbeinu Tam and Ri give distinct answers.
Issur recounts their former assumption and the rule of carrying a purse in successive intervals of less than four cubits. Rava quotes him.
The text names both business partners. The next verb for appearing before Rabbah bar Rav Huna is singular after the account of Safra’s division.
This witness names Mari bar Issur and his two sons, Mar Zutra and Rav Adda the elder. It supports the named branch without establishing the full plural genealogy.
The internal dossier names Rav Mari bar Issur and gives the Adda/Acha reading difference.

holds.reason: The academy clause has no explicit subject in the wording cited here. Context favors Rav Mari. The source’s compact clause and the existing pronoun are retained.
